```{python}
#| label: fig-rc-clamp
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "RC-triggered power-supply clamp: in normal operation, the capacitor is charged to $V_\\mathrm{DD}$, the inverter output is low, and the large clamp transistor $M_\\mathrm{ESD}$ is off. During a fast ESD-induced rise of $V_\\mathrm{DD}$, the RC node lags behind, the inverter output goes high, and $M_\\mathrm{ESD}$ shorts the rails for the duration of the event."

import schemdraw as sd
import schemdraw.elements as elm

sd.svgconfig.svg2 = False

with sd.Drawing(canvas='svg') as d:
    d.config(unit=2, fontsize=10)

    # rails
    d += elm.Line().endpoints((0, 6), (10, 6)).label('$V_\\mathrm{DD}$',
                                                     loc='left')
    d += elm.Line().endpoints((0, 0), (10, 0)).label('$V_\\mathrm{SS}$',
                                                     loc='left')

    # RC branch
    d += elm.Resistor().endpoints((2, 6), (2, 3.3)).label('$R$',
                                                          loc='bottom')
    d += elm.Capacitor().endpoints((2, 2.7), (2, 0)).label('$C$',
                                                           loc='bottom')
    d += elm.Line().endpoints((2, 3.3), (2, 2.7))
    d += elm.Dot().at((2, 3))
    d += elm.Dot().at((2, 6))
    d += elm.Dot().at((2, 0))

    # inverter
    d += elm.Line().endpoints((2, 3), (3.5, 3))
    d += elm.Line().endpoints((3.5, 3.8), (3.5, 2.2))
    d += elm.Line().endpoints((3.5, 3.8), (4.9, 3))
    d += elm.Line().endpoints((3.5, 2.2), (4.9, 3))
    d += elm.Dot(open=True, radius=0.1).at((5.0, 3))
    d += elm.Line().endpoints((5.1, 3), (6.2, 3))

    # clamp NMOS
    m = elm.NFet(bulk=False).at((6.2, 3)).anchor('gate').theta(0).reverse()
    d += m.label('$M_\\mathrm{ESD}$', loc='right', ofst=(-0.3, 0))
    d += elm.Line().at(m.drain).to((m.drain[0], 6))
    d += elm.Line().at(m.source).to((m.source[0], 0))
    d += elm.Dot().at((m.drain[0], 6))
    d += elm.Dot().at((m.source[0], 0))
```
